families.title: Carbon networks for Li-ion channels
families.blurb: Benzene rings joined by alkyne linkers, built to have pores a lithium ion can pass through; the _ions variants also map where Li+, Na+ and K+ sit and how easily they cross (liminal).

families.title: Carbon linkers that join themselves and each other
families.blurb: Rings, polyyne alkynes, trigonal sp2 carbon nodes and C3 units (allene, cyclopropenyl, propargyl), each able to bond its own kind as well as the others.

families.title: Graphyne and graphdiyne
families.blurb: The sp-sp2 carbon allotropes: benzene rings joined only through one alkyne (graphyne) or exactly two (graphdiyne), built as large amorphous 3D networks.

families.title: Covalent triazine frameworks
families.blurb: Triazine rings linked through phenylene, alkyne or mixed struts, in 60 A cells sized for a Slurm node.

families.title: Porous aromatic frameworks
families.blurb: Tetrahedral nodes, a single sp3 carbon as in PAF-1 or an adamantane cage, joined through biphenyl struts: 3D by construction, with very high surface areas.

families.title: sp3-sp2 networks
families.blurb: Every sp3 carbon a pre-built tetraphenylmethane node with four phenyl (sp2) arms, joined through phenylene struts or into an sp2 network of rings and trigonal carbons. The sp3 centres break conjugation, so these recipes also measure the pi network's gap and conductance, with and without tunnelling through them (liminal).
